trigger.reportedFixedEndpointResult: Both loopback lockdown connects timed out before TCP readiness; no bytes received.
trigger.interpretation: This closes only the tested fixed-endpoint experiment for the recorded conditions. The waiting POSIX code is not a proven denial mechanism or proof against every transport.

recommendedSmallestSlice.name: bounded-same-device-RemotePairing-discovery-and-connect-only
recommendedSmallestSlice.implementationLocation: Extend the existing original Network.framework diagnostic service with a separate discovery stage; do not vendor upstream implementation.
steps: Capture a bounded numeric snapshot of the current device interface addresses, preserving IPv6 scope identifiers, without exporting those addresses.
Browse only _remotepairing._tcp in local. with a fixed overall deadline and result cap. Do not enumerate all service types, publish a host service, or send custom multicast packets.
Resolve candidate service addresses and SRV port through a DNS-SD resolver before creating TCP connections. NWBrowser loopback metadata is a hint, not an ownership proof.

Accept only valid numeric unicast addresses equal to addresses on the captured local non-VPN interface snapshot, or explicitly classified loopback. Reject unknown hosts, peer routes, wildcard, multicast and broadcast values. Preserve and validate IPv6 link-local scope. Do not substitute a peer or fallback address.

Revalidate address ownership immediately before connecting; use only the numeric approved address and discovered port, never the service hostname or unresolved service endpoint. Stop if the interface snapshot changed or no candidate is provably local.
Attempt only a bounded TCP open to those approved same-device candidates, then close without sending an application frame. Never send lockdown QueryType to a RemotePairing listener.

Export counts, candidate origin category, stage, deadline outcome and normalized errors only. Distinguish discovery unavailable, no same-device candidate, resolution failure, connect waiting, connect timeout and actual TCP-ready. Keep renewalProven and all TLS/session/pair/account/sign/install flags false.
recommendedSmallestSlice.evidenceMeaning: A TCP-ready result establishes only a reachable local address and discovered port. Service identity, same-daemon identity and an authenticated usable transport remain unverified.
recommendedSmallestSlice.inferenceBoundary: Local address equality establishes the destination locality under the current interface snapshot, not cryptographic peer identity. A local proxy or system routing behavior is not excluded.

pureSelectionFixtureCases: only declared service type and valid SRV ports are accepted
a loopback hint plus a nonlocal resolved address is rejected
a same-device candidate is never replaced by another LAN service
IPv4 and IPv6 canonicalization and scoped link-local equality
wildcard, broadcast, multicast, empty, malformed and oversized input rejection
DNS rebinding or interface ownership change before connect yields no connect
bounded duplicate results, removals, result cap, deadline and cancellation races
connection waiting remains distinct from ready or terminal failed
report redaction excludes names, addresses, TXT and raw payloads
sourceOnlyVerification.SDKFixtureTests: Inject discovery, interface snapshot, resolver, clock and TCP adapters. Test single completion, teardown and late callbacks on the existing iOS Simulator test target; simulator tests are not local-network privacy or device acceptance.
sourceOnlyVerification.DNSResolverSDKBoundary: The chosen system DNS-SD resolver and numeric-address adapter still need compile/link and availability checks against the actual iOS SDK and deployment target. Windows source inspection cannot establish their runtime availability or behavior on this iOS version; same-device discovery and local-network privacy require a physical device.

devicePrerequisitesAndUnknowns: A future foreground probe needs its exact Bonjour service in NSBonjourServices and an appropriate localized NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription. No such plist change was made here.
Bonjour browsing and resolution require the local-network privilege. Permission state, denial and no advertisement must not be inferred from an empty result alone.
Whether this iOS version advertises its own RemotePairing service to a sandboxed app, and whether its SRV addresses can be proven local without pairing input, is unknown.
Whether direct TCP to the discovered same-device endpoint can become ready without a VPN, companion app or computer is unknown; the supplied fixed lockdown report did not test this.

Even if discovery and TCP pass, read-only authentication needs a separately bounded design and an existing locally provisioned pairing record. Do not read a pairing record merely to make this discovery stage run.
No source inspection, simulator fixture or bare TCP result proves fresh provisioning, signing, replacement installation, preserved data or unattended/expiry recovery.

applePrimaryReference.facts: Specific Bonjour browsing/resolution requires local-network access, NSBonjourServices and a usage description. Browsing all types or arbitrary multicast has additional entitlement requirements, so this proposal does neither. Simulator does not support local-network privacy; test that behavior on a device. A waiting state is not an established denial cause for the existing report.

sourceEvidence.finding: The RemotePairing endpoint port is discovered through Bonjour. Loopback is a preferred candidate, not a mandatory restriction. User override and last-discovered values also exist at lines 22-30.

The one-shot resolver browses one requested type but falls back from a loopback-preferred candidate to any matched service at line 806. It initiates NWConnection before any local-address ownership check and accepts path information in both ready and waiting. This helper cannot be reused as a strict same-device transport gate.
The application declares RemotePairing Bonjour service types and a local-network usage description. Its broad service list is not needed for a single-service probe.
49152 is a default RemotePairing port, while _remotepairing._tcp. is the daemon discovery service type. Neither the default port nor its presence proves reachability on this iPhone.
The exact IDevice binary target references release v0.1.68-ss-3e55c84 and its package checksum. This is the actual lower-level revision, not an assumed current idevice branch.
The normal RemotePairing tunnel path uses an existing RP pairing file and passes pair_if_needed=false. It is an authenticated step beyond discovery or a bare TCP connection.
Raw RemotePairing uses a direct TCP stream and RpPairingSocket, then invokes authenticated connection and tunnel creation. A lockdown QueryType frame is not the protocol for this service.
After authentication, the TLS tunnel listener port is negotiated; RSD port and internal addressing come from the tunnel handshake. An outer TCP success alone proves none of those later steps.
The VPN implementation configures NEPacketTunnelProvider routes and swaps and reinjects packetFlow packets. Copying its peer-address defaults would not establish an equivalent direct route.
